findings.problem: Accept/serving JoinHandles are discarded; H2/H3/TLS returned errors are unobserved and H1 read/write errors are collapsed into loop termination. Healthy client assertions do not collect every peer outcome.
findings.qualification: The dedicated Origin Runtime bounds task lifetime on runtime destruction; this is completed-error retention evidence, not a claim of a permanent leak.
findings.proposal: Acquire concrete task owners at spawn, retain completed results and JoinErrors, and explicitly collect all peers alongside the request primary. A real healthy request before a distinct post-operation worker fault can prove the missing cause boundary.

findings.problem: Server Drop aborts only its accept task; accepted children remain detached. Spawned request handles and the separate TLS accept task cross later fallible operations or by-value timeouts without a cleanup owner.
findings.qualification: Drop requests cancellation without awaiting it. Source does not establish natural leakage, unbounded lifetime, or a production defect; the enclosing integration runtime can later destroy tasks.
findings.proposal: Use concrete eager guards for acquired tasks and accepted descendants. Observe actual pending read/handshake plus child destruction and socket closure before an independent finite backup. Keep completed external cancellation/panic failures; suppress only cancellation explicitly requested for pending cleanup.

findings.problem: Four timeout mappings discard the original Tokio Elapsed and return text only.
findings.qualification: Other timeout uses that propagate Elapsed and quiet-window expiry used as a successful negative observation are separate contracts.
findings.proposal: Keep the current periods and literal messages in a private typed error with original Elapsed source. Test actual original future Pending before expiry, ready success and exact inner-error preservation.

findings.problem: Local support aliases precede standard/external imports; btls/tokio_btls imports follow the Tokio block in the parallel owner.
findings.qualification: Mechanical standards grouping only; no behavioral failure follows from the ordering.
findings.proposal: Place standard, external and local groups consistently without changing operation bodies.

observation_qualifications: Quiet-window request admission checks spawn a task then time its JoinHandle without an independent actual request-future Pending witness. This is an observation-strength gap, not a demonstrated false positive. Add a wrapper that polls the original send future and signals actual Pending before starting the existing quiet interval.

Runtime counts increment at actual accepted TCP/QUIC arrival, not completed authentication; successful status/body requests independently establish the healthy path. The kept current-thread runtime is intentionally retained without further driving, rather than secretly running in the background.

The scoped thread is joined by std::thread::scope on every scope exit; its request has its own finite timeout. The panic mapping at runtimes.rs:363 loses the original panic payload, but no panic was observed.

The two-second idle sleep is an explicit elapsed idle-policy trigger with a real replacement connection and original socket EOF assertion. It is not a readiness barrier. No platform reset classification waiver is proposed without a separate concrete witness.

The TLS cancellation case witnesses actual accepted TCP streams and actual cancelled request JoinHandles; it does not observe parsed ClientHello or canonical handshake Pending. The later healthy responses and accepted indices are real positives.
The custom-profile debug-string assertion checks applied configuration representation only. It is not three-request admission evidence, and no ignored production setting is inferred.
